Jaipal & Ors. Cnr No.: Dlse01-004908-2018 1. Mohd. Saleem Ahmad S/o Md. Sageer Ahmad R/o 2943/35, Tughlakabad Extn., New Delhi. .....Petitioner Versus 1. Sh. Jaipal S/o Sh. Ranglal R/o Village-Shimla Khetri PS-Khetri, Distt-Jhunjhunu Rajasthan. ............Driver/Respondent no.1 2. Dtc Manager Central Workshop-I, B.B. Marg, Delhi-110009. ............Owner/Respondent no.2 3. United India Insurance Company Ltd. D.O.-Ii, New Delhi,D.O. Xi Mact No.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 1 Of 22 Bk E-85, Himalya House, 23, K.G. Marg New Delhi. ........Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Date of accident : 14.02.2011 Result of accident : Injury(Permanent disability) Date of filing of Petition : 03.03.2012 Date of Decision : 30.04.2025 Award 1. Pursuant to order dated 29.11.2024, passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, Award initially passed by learned Predecessor of this Tribunal dated 19.11.2019 has been [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the matter has been remanded for assessment of compensation in accordance with law.
texts.facts: Brief facts of the case are that on 14.02.2011 at about 5 pm, petitioner/injured Mohd. Saleem Ahmad (aged 19 years) was driving his motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SBE-4179, from Tara Apartment, Delhi to Ravidas Marg. While taking a turn from Ravidas Marg, he was hit by rashly and negligently driven DTC bus bearing no. DL-1PB-6407(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle). As an impact of the collision, petitioner fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries. On a call to 100 number, PCR van reached at the spot and took the injured to Jai Prakash Narain Apex Trauma Center AIIMS for treatment. 3. An FIR no.48/2011 was registered u/s 279,338 of IPC PS Govindpuri. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 2 Of 22 BK 4. Respondent no.1 is driver, Respondent no.2 is owner of the offending vehicle. Respondent no.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 5. Written statement filed on behalf of Respondent no.1 denying negligence on his part while alleging that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner who was driving a motorcycle without having a valid driving licence and lost his balance causing the injuries to him. Respondent no.1 pleaded that he was having valid driving licence and offending vehicle was insured with respondent no.3. Respondent no.2 filed written statement stating therein that offending vehicle was duly insured with United India Insurance company. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed its reply submitting that there is delay of 18 days in arrest the driver of the offending vehicle. However, it admitted that offending vehicle was insured on the date of accident. 6. Vide order dated 06.02.2013, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the petitioner suffered injuries in a road vehicular accident that took place on 14.02.2011 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing registration no.DL-1PB-6407 by respondent no.1? 3. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner Mohd. Saleem Ahmed led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1 by way of affidavit MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 3 Of 22 BK as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the claim petition. He further deposed that he was tutor by Md. Saleem Ahmad vs Jaipal on 30 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32394244/ 2 profession and earning Rs.12,000/- p.m. He spent Rs.16,95,174/- on account medical treatment, Rs.1,50,000/- on conveyance, Rs.4,60,000/- on attendant. He suffered diaphragmatic tear with pelvic fracture with urethral injury with mesenteric tear with veicocutaneous, rectovesicle and rectocutaneous fistula and also remained under treatment for his Urology problem. He relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1, PAN card as Ex.PW-1/2, chargesheet as Ex.PW-1/3, education certificate as Ex.PW-1/4, IGNOU I card as Ex.PW-1/5, Medical bills of Rs.16,95,174/- as Ex.PW-1/6, Medical bills as Ex.PW-1/7, Medical prescription as Ex.PW-1/8. He was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/Respondent no.3. Further, PW-1 also led additional evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A1. He relied upon original medical bills of Rs.79,151/- as Ex.PW-1/9(colly). He was cross- examined by learned counsel for insurance company. PW-1 tendered his learner license and discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/10. He was not cross-examined by any of the respondent no.2/insurance company. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company. Relevant portion of the order is reproduced hereunder: "...9. 10. Pertinently, the Appellant who appeared as PW1, had cogently deposed that he was going on his motorcycle when the offending vehicle bearing No.DL-1PB-6407 driven in a rash and negligent manner by Sh. Jaipal, Respondent no.1, came at a high speed being and hit his motorcycle causing the accident. The evidence of the Appellant explained how the accident was caused due to sole negligence of the Respondent/Driver of the offending vehicle. Md. Saleem Ahmad vs Jaipal on 30 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32394244/ 3 11. The Respondents, including the Driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged the testimony of the Injured. The circumstances as explained by the Injured, do not spell any circumstance which could attribute the negligence to the injured. 12. Further, the Chargesheet Ex.PW 1/3 has been filed against the Driver of the Offending Bus. As the entitlement to compensation to the petitioner who was MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 6 Of 22 BK himself injured, has not been questioned by the insurance company or any of the respondents, injured is entitled to compensation.
texts.arguments: However, the Apex Court has held in Saraswati Palariya & Ors. vs. The New India Assurance Company Ltd. & Ors., Civil Appeal No.9114/2018, that merely because a vehicle was being driven by the deceased without a Driving License, would not ipso facto establish Negligence. In the case of National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rai 2009 MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 5 Of 22 BK ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been held that filing of Chargesheet is sufficient proof of the negligence and involvement of the Offending Vehicle. 13. While considering this aspect of negligence, it must not be forgotten that it is a compensation case under M.V. Act which is under consideration and unless there is some independent evidence to show that the injured di not know how to drive the motorcycle or had committed any act which contributed or would be attributable to his lack of skill of driving of motorcycle, mere absence of Driving License or just holding a Learner's Licence, cannot be a ground to conclude that the Appellant was sole negligent in causing the accident. 14. 12. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding Md. Saleem Ahmad vs Jaipal on 30 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32394244/ 4 damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 13. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 7 Of 22 BK following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 13.1. 13.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 13.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 8 Of 22 BK under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve Md. Saleem Ahmad vs Jaipal on 30 April, 2025 13.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: If the MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 9 Of 22 BK claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry. 25. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 17 Of 22 BK the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to MACT NO.618/21 Md. Saleem Ahmad v. Jaipal P.No. 18 Of 22 BK ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
